purpose: D2 — within the 32-frame per-stream write buffer capacity (no overflow expected), to observe write-executor/write-duration behavior under sustained slow-client backpressure without triggering fail-fast.

gateway_log_timeline.note: same JVM process as overflow-scenario, run immediately after; no restart between scenarios

finding: The slow client's TCP-level backpressure propagates into a blocking PrintWriter.write()+flush() call taking up to ~0.605s (servlet_write_duration_seconds_max), with the write executor thread genuinely occupied (active=1) for part of the request. The bounded per-stream buffer provided runway (peaked at 8/32, well below capacity) rather than growing unbounded — consistent with the overflow-scenario's fail-fast design engaging only once actual capacity is exceeded.
notes: Diagnostic only. Not a performance measurement — no comparison implied against P3-C's handling of the same workload.
